title: Understanding SBP Payments After a Military Retiree Dies (November 2026)
summary: See how SBP, VA DIC, and Social Security survivor benefits work together for military families after a retiree's death in 2026.
body_markdown:
After a military retiree dies, eligible beneficiaries may receive monthly income from the Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP), a Department of Defense annuity administered by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS). SBP is separate from VA survivor benefits and Social Security survivor benefits, and each program has its own claim. This guide explains key points for surviving spouses and executors to be aware of, including: who is eligible for SBP, how payments are calculated, which forms start an annuity, how SBP works alongside VA DIC and Social Security, and more.


**Key Takeaways**


- SBP pays eligible spouses 55% of the retiree's elected base amount each month.
- SBP claims require DD Form 2656-7 and supporting records.
- Since 2023, eligible surviving spouses can generally receive both SBP and VA DIC in full.
- SBP, VA DIC, and Social Security survivor benefits each require a separate claim.
- Elayne Asset Search organizes potential military survivor benefits into an estate inventory.


## What Is the Survivor Benefit Plan?


The Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) provides monthly income to an eligible surviving spouse or other covered beneficiary after a military retiree dies. It is a Department of Defense annuity, or recurring payment, administered by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS).


For spouses, the[monthly SBP benefit amount](https://militarypay.defense.gov/Benefits/Survivor-Benefit-Plan/Costs-and-Benefits/Spouse-Coverage/) is 55% of the retiree’s elected base amount: the retired pay selected for coverage.


SBP, Social Security survivor benefits, and VA survivor benefits are separate programs. Families may qualify through multiple agencies, each reviewing eligibility separately.

## Who Is Eligible to Receive SBP Payments


Survivor Benefit Plan eligibility depends on the retiree’s elected coverage and beneficiary circumstances:


- A surviving spouse generally qualifies after one year of marriage, or sooner if the couple had a child.
- A former spouse requires former-spouse coverage.
- Unmarried dependent children generally qualify under 18, or under 22 as full-time students. Disability exceptions can extend eligibility.
- A named person with an insurable interest may qualify under that coverage.


Under the Department of Defense's spouse remarriage rules, spouse payments stop upon remarriage before 55 but can resume if that marriage ends. Remarriage at 55 or older does not interrupt payments.


## How an SBP Annuity Starts After a Retiree Dies


1. The death is reported to DFAS, separate from the process to[report a death to the VA](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-notify-the-va-of-a-veterans-death) .
2. The beneficiary completes DD Form 2656-7, Verification for Survivor Annuity, using the wizard on the[DFAS annuity application page](https://www.dfas.mil/RetiredMilitary/survivors/ApplySBP/) .
3. The signed form is submitted with supporting documents, including the death certificate and, for spouse claims, marriage certificate.


Reporting the death alone does not start SBP payments. DFAS must review the claim; timing varies, and families can request a status update.


## How SBP Payments Are Calculated


SBP payments depend on the elected base amount, which can range from $300 to full retired pay under the Department of Defense's SBP benefit payment rules. Example monthly payments before taxes:


Elected base amount Monthly SBP payment


$1,000 $550


$2,000 $1,100


$3,000 $1,650


Figures shown are pre-COLA estimates at enrollment.


SBP replaces part of the retiree’s income and provides inflation-adjusted monthly survivor income through cost-of-living adjustments. A survivor benefit plan calculator can estimate payments, but DFAS confirms the amount payable under the retiree’s coverage.


## SBP and VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation


VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) is one of several[veterans benefits after death](https://www.elayne.com/resources/veterans-benefits-after-death) and is separate from the Survivor Benefit Plan. Eligibility can follow a service-connected death or a qualifying period of total service-connected disability.


The former dollar-for-dollar SBP reduction ended January 1, 2023. DFAS’s[SBP and DIC guidance](https://www.dfas.mil/retiredmilitary/survivors/Understanding-SBP-DIC-SSIA/) explains eligibility:


- [2026 DIC base rate](https://www.va.gov/family-and-caregiver-benefits/survivor-compensation/dependency-indemnity-compensation/survivor-rates/) : $1,699.36 monthly.
- An additional payment applies under the 8-year provision when the veteran was rated totally disabled by VA (including through individual unemployability) for at least that many full years immediately before death and the spouse was married to the veteran throughout that period.
- Effective December 1, 2025, for eligible spouses of veterans who died on or after January 1, 1993.


Eligible surviving spouses can receive both benefits in full.


## Social Security Survivor Benefits for Military Families


Social Security reviews survivor claims separately from DFAS and VA, under its own[social security survivor benefits](https://www.elayne.com/resources/social-security-benefits-for-a-deceased-spouse-what-you-need-to-know) rules. Surviving spouses generally qualify:


- At 60, or 50 with a qualifying disability.
- At any age while caring for the deceased worker’s eligible child under 16.


Spouse payments generally range from 71.5% to 100% of the worker’s benefit, depending on claiming age. Spouses generally receive the higher of their own or survivor benefit.


June 2026 SSA figures show an average of roughly $1,931 monthly for the combined category of aged widow(er)s and aged parents, not a widow(er)-only average. That average is not a guaranteed payment; individual amounts depend on earnings records.

## How Elayne Helps Families Identify and Organize Military Survivor Benefits


Military survivor benefits are one of several income streams a family may need to identify after a retiree dies. SBP, VA DIC, and Social Security survivor benefits are each claimed through a different agency, and each agency reviews eligibility separately. Accounts, insurance policies, pensions, and benefits are recorded by different institutions, and a will is not an inventory of accounts. Elayne Asset Search looks for accounts, debts, and veterans benefits connected to the person who died, then organizes the findings into an estate inventory.


The search starts with IRS tax transcripts. A tax transcript is not a tax return. The document records what banks, employers, insurers, and other institutions reported about the person to the IRS over 10 years. Elayne holds IRS authorization to request these transcripts.


For example, an entry may name a bank, a brokerage, an insurance company, or a retirement account custodian, each of which may have an account or policy connected to the person. Identity verification for the request often involves the person's Social Security number, covered in this guide on[how to find a deceased person's SSN](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-get-a-deceased-persons-social-security-number) .


More than 100 other sources are checked in the same search, including:


- The person's Equifax credit report, which lists open accounts, debts, cards, and credit lines in the person's name.
- Life insurance locators, which cover in-force and lapsed policies.
- The pension registry, which lists unclaimed pensions from terminated plans.
- The national unclaimed property database and state unclaimed property searches.
- Property and vehicle records, including deeds, mortgages, liens, and titled vehicles.
- Crypto exchange accounts, when the tax transcripts or estate record point to crypto.
- Veterans benefits and VA life insurance records, including unclaimed veterans insurance funds, when the estate record shows veteran status.


Each finding is added to the estate inventory with the institution or record that reported the information. Debts appear next to assets, so the inventory shows what the estate owes as well as what the person owned. The transcripts also show whether the estate owes the IRS anything. An Estate Expert then walks through the findings in a 1:1 call.


Some items fall outside the search, including safe deposit boxes, physical assets, and private loans. A search documents what was found and where the information came from, and cannot guarantee that every account or benefit will be found. Each military survivor benefit still requires a separate claim with the agency that administers the program: DFAS for SBP, the VA for DIC, and the Social Security Administration for survivor benefits. Reporting a death to one agency does not start a claim with another.


Elayne Asset Search is an eligible estate expense, paid from the estate or reimbursed by the estate. Family members and attorneys can be invited to work from the same estate record.


## FAQ


### Can a Survivor Benefit Plan calculator estimate payments without the retiree’s coverage election?


No. A Survivor Benefit Plan calculator needs the elected base amount; using full retired pay could overstate expected income if the retiree selected reduced coverage. DFAS can confirm the coverage election and benefit amount before a family builds a budget around the estimate.


### Can beneficiaries follow up with DFAS when Survivor Benefit Plan payments have not started?


Beneficiaries can request a claim status update from DFAS. A useful follow-up confirms whether the signed annuity application and supporting documents were received, whether anything is missing, and whether a payment amount or start date has been approved.


### How can a military retiree's death be reported to DFAS?


A death can be reported through the askDFAS online Notification of Death form, or by calling DFAS. Reports can also be faxed or mailed. The online form asks for the retiree's full name, Social Security number, date of death, cause of death, and marital status. A spouse also provides the date of marriage. DFAS stops monthly retired pay once the death is reported.


### What documents does DFAS use to start an SBP annuity?


DFAS starts an SBP annuity with a signed and dated DD Form 2656-7 (Verification for Survivor Annuity) and supporting documents. Those documents include IRS Form W-4P for federal tax withholding, a direct deposit enrollment form, and a copy of the retiree's death certificate showing the cause of death if DFAS does not already have one. Other documents apply in specific situations, such as a custodianship certificate for a minor claimant. Completed forms can be uploaded through the askDFAS online tool, mailed, or faxed.
